claim: Synaptic plasticity is a cardinal cellular mechanism for learning and memory.
source: Synaptic plasticity is a cardinal cellular mechanism for learning and memory.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus in the field of neuroscience.

claim: The endocannabinoid (eCB) system has emerged as a pivotal pathway for synaptic plasticity because of its widely characterized ability to depress synaptic transmission on short- and long-term scales.
source: The endocannabinoid (eCB) system has emerged as a pivotal pathway for synaptic plasticity because of its widely characterized ability to depress synaptic transmission on short- and long-term scales.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about the eCB system's role in synaptic depression.

claim: Recent reports indicate that eCBs also mediate potentiation of the synapse.
source: Recent reports indicate that eCBs also mediate potentiation of the synapse.
evidence: This refers to recent literature findings about eCB-mediated potentiation.

claim: STDP outcome is controlled by eCB levels and dynamics.
source: We demonstrate that STDP outcome is controlled by eCB levels and dynamics: prolonged and moderate levels of eCB lead to eCB-mediated long-term depression (eCB-tLTD) while short and large eCB transients produce eCB-mediated long-term potentiation (eCB-tLTP).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data and modeling presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Prolonged and moderate levels of eCB lead to eCB-mediated long-term depression (eCB-tLTD).
source: prolonged and moderate levels of eCB lead to eCB-mediated long-term depression (eCB-tLTD)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from 2-AG puff experiments and STDP protocols shown in Figures 6 and throughout the manuscript.

claim: Short and large eCB transients produce eCB-mediated long-term potentiation (eCB-tLTP).
source: short and large eCB transients produce eCB-mediated long-term potentiation (eCB-tLTP)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from 2-AG puff experiments and STDP protocols shown in Figures 6 and throughout the manuscript.

claim: eCB-tLTD requires active calcineurin.
source: Moreover, we show that eCB-tLTD requires active calcineurin
evidence: This is supported by pharmacological experiments with cyclosporin A shown in Figure 10.

claim: eCB-tLTP necessitates the activity of presynaptic PKA.
source: eCB-tLTP necessitates the activity of presynaptic PKA
evidence: This is supported by pharmacological experiments with PKA inhibitors shown in Figure 10.

claim: Endocannabinoids form a bidirectional system to encode learning and memory, just like glutamate or GABA.
source: Therefore, just like glutamate or GABA, eCB form a bidirectional system to encode learning and memory.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and modeling results presented in the study.

claim: Bidirectional long-term plasticity of synaptic strength (LTD and LTP) underlies multiple forms of learning and memory.
source: Bidirectional long-term plasticity of synaptic strength (LTD and LTP) underlies multiple forms of learning and memory (Citri and Malenka, 2008; Nabavi et al, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Bidirectionality allows LTP and LTD to reverse each other with time at a single synapse, thus enabling adaptive changes of the synaptic weight.
source: Bidirectionality is of paramount functional importance since it allows LTP and LTD to reverse each other with time at a single synapse, thus enabling adaptive changes of the synaptic weight.
evidence: This is an inference based on established understanding of synaptic plasticity mechanisms.

claim: Endocannabinoids have emerged as a major actor in learning and memory because of their powerful influence on synaptic plasticity.
source: Endocannabinoids (eCBs) have emerged as a major actor in learning and memory because of their powerful influence on synaptic plasticity (Chevaleyre et al., 2006; Heifets and Castillo, 2009; Kano et al., 2009; Katona and Freund, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: The eCB system is mainly composed of active biolipids (notably 2-arachidonylglycerol, 2-AG and anandamide, AEA) synthesized and released on-demand acting as retrograde neurotransmitters on presynaptic type-1 cannabinoid receptor (CB1R) and postsynaptic transient receptor potential vanilloid-type-1 (TRPV1).
source: The eCB system is mainly composed of active biolipids (notably 2-arachidonylglycerol, 2-AG and anandamide, AEA) synthesized and released on-demand acting as retrograde neurotransmitters on presynaptic type-1 cannabinoid receptor (CB1R) and postsynaptic transient receptor potential vanilloid-type-1 (TRPV1) (Piomelli, 2003; Piomelli et al., 2007; Di Marzo, 2008; Alger and Kim, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the eCB system supported by citations.

claim: The major neurotransmitter systems, glutamate and GABA, allow bidirectional synaptic plasticity.
source: The major neurotransmitter systems, glutamate and GABA, allow bidirectional synaptic plasticity (Citri and Malenka, 2008)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: eCBs have been widely described as a powerful unidirectional system that depresses neuronal communication on a short or long timescale.
source: In contrast, eCBs have been widely described as a powerful unidirectional system that depresses neuronal communication on a short or long timescale.
evidence: This refers to the prevailing view in the literature prior to recent findings.

claim: An eCB-mediated spike-timing dependent LTP exists in the dorsal striatum induced by a low number of paired stimulations and dependent on the activation of CB1R and TRPV1.
source: We recently reported the existence of an eCB-mediated spike-timing dependent LTP in the dorsal striatum induced by a low number of paired stimulations and dependent on the activation of CB1R and TRPV1 (Cui et al, 2015).
evidence: This refers to a previous publication by the authors.

claim: Few coincident pre- and post-synaptic spikes (5–15) are sufficient to increase synaptic efficacy through a signaling pathway that relies on the activation of CB1R and TRPV1 and on 2-AG elevations.
source: We found that few coincident pre- and post-synaptic spikes (5–15) were sufficient to increase synaptic efficacy through a signaling pathway that relies on the activation of CB1R and TRPV1 and on 2-AG elevations.
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study by the authors (Cui et al, 2015).

claim: 2-AG elevations are triggered by coupled postsynaptic rises of calcium and DAG lipase α (DAGLα) activity mediated by type-5 metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluR5), muscarinic M1 receptors and voltage-sensitive calcium channels (VSCCs).
source: The latter are triggered by coupled postsynaptic rises of calcium and DAG lipase α (DAGLα) activity mediated by type-5 metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluR5), muscarinic M1 receptors and voltage-sensitive calcium channels (VSCCs) (Cui et al, 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study by the authors.

claim: An indirect role of eCBs in promoting LTP at mixed (chemical and electrical) synapses of the goldfish Mauthner cell via intermediary dopaminergic neurons has been reported.
source: In addition, it has been reported an indirect role of eCBs in promoting LTP at mixed (chemical and electrical) synapses of the goldfish Mauthner cell via intermediary dopaminergic neurons (Cachope et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: eCBs promote LTP at hippocampal CA1 synapses via a GABAA receptor-mediated mechanism.
source: or at hippocampal CA1 synapses via a GABAA receptor-mediated mechanism (Lin et al., 2011; Xu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Facilitation of LTP in the hippocampus via eCB-induced presynaptic depression of GABAergic transmission has been reported.
source: Likewise, facilitation of LTP in the hippocampus via eCB-induced presynaptic depression of GABAergic transmission (Carlson et al., 2002; Chevaleyre and Castillo, 2004; Zhu and Lovinger, 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mediation of heterosynaptic short-term potentiation via intermediary astrocytes has been reported.
source: and mediation of heterosynaptic short-term potentiation via intermediary astrocytes (Navarrete and Araque, 2010) have been reported.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The principal mechanism put forward to account for bidirectionality in glutamate signaling is the calcium-control hypothesis, which states that postsynaptic calcium levels and/or time courses decide the outcome of plasticity (LTP or LTD).
source: In the case of glutamate, the principal mechanism put forward to account for bidirectionality is the calcium-control hypothesis, which states that postsynaptic calcium levels and/or time courses decide the outcome of plasticity (LTP or LTD) (Shouval et al., 2002; Graupner and Brunel, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The bidirectionality of eCB-dependent STDP in striatum is controlled by eCB-levels: moderate level and prolonged release of eCB lead to LTD while brief releases of high eCB concentration yield LTP.
source: Here, combining experimental and computer modeling approaches, we show that the bidirectionality of eCB-dependent STDP in striatum is controlled by eCB-levels: moderate level and prolonged release of eCB lead to LTD while brief releases of high eCB concentration yield LTP.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data and modeling.

claim: MAG-lipase appears as a key controller of synaptic plasticity.
source: In this aspect, MAG-lipase appears as a key controller of synaptic plasticity.
evidence: This is inferred from experimental results showing that MAGL inhibition modulates plasticity outcomes.

claim: 100 post-pre pairings (-30<ΔtSTDP<0 ms) induced tLTP (mean value of the EPSC amplitude recorded 50 min after STDP protocol: 156±15%, p=0.0015, n=19).
source: post-pre pairings (-30<ΔtSTDP<0 ms) induced tLTP (mean value of the EPSC amplitude recorded 50 min after STDP protocol: 156±15%, p=0.0015, n=19)
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: 100 pre-post pairings (0<ΔtSTDP<+30 ms) induced tLTD (76±8%, p=0.0051, n=11).
source: while pre-post pairings (0<ΔtSTDP<+30 ms) induced tLTD (76±8%, p=0.0051, n=11)
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The corticostriatal STDP displays an anti-hebbian polarity in accordance with previous reports.
source: Note that this STDP displays an anti-hebbian polarity in accordance with previous reports (Fino et al., 2005; Fino et al., 2010; Schulz et al., 2010; Paillé et al., 2013; Cui et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature and the current experimental observations.

claim: GABA acts as an Hebbian/anti-Hebbian switch at corticostriatal synapses.
source: We have previously shown that GABA acts as an Hebbian/anti-Hebbian switch (Paillé et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: The polarity of the corticostriatal STDP depends on whether GABAA receptor antagonists are applied.
source: so polarity of the corticostriatal STDP depends on whether GABAA receptor antagonists are applied (Hebbian STDP; Pawlak and Kerr, 2008; Shen et al., 2008) or not (anti-Hebbian STDP; Fino et al., 2005; Fino et al., 2010; Fino and Venance, 2010; Cui et al., 2015; this study).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature and current study observations.

claim: tLTP induced by 100 post-pre pairings was NMDAR-mediated since blocked by the selective NMDAR blocker D-AP5 (50 μM) (99±3%, p=0.7998, n=4).
source: tLTP was NMDAR-mediated since blocked by the selective NMDAR blocker D-AP5 (50 μM) (99±3%, p=0.7998, n=4)
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 1C2.

claim: tLTD induced by 100 pre-post pairings relied on eCBs because pharmacological inhibition of CB1R with AM251 (3 μM) impaired this plasticity (102±7%, p=0.8108, n=4).
source: while tLTD relied on eCBs because pharmacological inhibition of CB1R with AM251 (3 μM) impaired this plasticity (102±7%, p=0.8108, n=4)
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 1D2.

claim: Lowering the number of pairings down to 10 yields tLTP for post-pre pairings (163±12%, p<0.0001, n=25).
source: As recently reported (Cui et al., 2015), lowering the number of pairings down to 10 yields tLTP for post-pre pairings (163±12%, p<0.0001, n=25)
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: 10 pre-post pairings result in a lack of significant plasticity (97±11%, p=0.3844, n=8).
source: and a lack of significant plasticity for pre-post pairings (97±11%, p=0.3844, n=8).
evidence: This is experimental data.

claim: tLTP induced with 10 post-pre STDP pairings was CB1R-mediated since treatment with AM251 (3 μM) resulted in an absence of significant plasticity (88±11%, p=0.3073, n=5).
source: tLTP induced with 10 post-pre STDP pairings was CB1R-mediated since treatment with AM251 (3 μM) resulted in an absence of significant plasticity (88±11%, p=0.3073, n=5)
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 1E2.

claim: The locus of eCB-tLTP maintenance is presynaptic.
source: Location of CB1R at the presynaptic terminals of the corticostriatal pathway (Katona and Freund, 2012) suggests that the locus of eCB-tLTP maintenance would likely be presynaptic.
evidence: This is inferred from the known location of CB1R and supported by experimental data in Figure 1F-H.

claim: A significant decrease of the paired-pulse facilitation (PPF) after STDP pairings (PPFplasticity/baseline=0.872±0.044, p=0.0470, n=14) indicates a presynaptic locus of eCB-tLTP.
source: We observed a significant decrease of the PPF after the STDP pairings (PPFplasticity/baseline=0.872±0.044, p=0.0470, n=14) (Figure 1F), which indicates a presynaptic locus of eCB-tLTP.
evidence: This is experimental data from paired-pulse experiments shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Mean variance analysis of EPSCs showed a CV-2 value of 3.6 ± 0.6 (p=0.0008, n=17), which confirmed a presynaptic maintenance of eCB-tLTP.
source: Second, using the mean variance analysis of EPSCs, we found a CV-2 value of 3.6 ± 0.6 (p=0.0008, n=17), which confirmed a presynaptic maintenance of eCB-tLTP (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is experimental data from variance analysis shown in Figure 1G.

claim: eCB-tLTP is maintained by a mechanism located downstream of CB1R activation in the presynaptic terminals.
source: This indicates that eCB-tLTP is maintained by a mechanism located downstream of CB1R activation in the presynaptic terminals.
evidence: This is inferred from experiments where AM251 applied after STDP pairings did not prevent tLTP (Figure 1H).

claim: NMDAR-tLTP is CaMKII-dependent since pharmacological inhibition of CaMKII with KN62 (3 µM) blocked NMDAR-tLTP (88 ± 11%, p=0.3324, n=6).
source: NMDAR-tLTP is CaMKII-dependent since we found that pharmacological inhibition of CaMKII with KN62 (3 µM) blocked NMDAR-tLTP (88 ± 11%, p=0.3324, n=6) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mathematical model combines a first signaling pathway leading from NMDAR to calmodulin and CaMKII with a second pathway that assembles mGluR and cytosolic calcium to eCB production and the resulting activation of CB1R.
source: We thus combined in the model a first signaling pathway leading from NMDAR to calmodulin and CaMKII with a second, distinct one that assembles mGluR and cytosolic calcium to eCB production and the resulting activation of CB1R (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the structure of the mathematical model shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In the model, the total synaptic weight (Wtotal) is given by the product of presynaptic (Wpre) and postsynaptic (Wpost) contributions.
source: In the model, the total synaptic weight (Wtotal) is given by the product of presynaptic (Wpre) and postsynaptic (Wpost) contributions (see Methods).
evidence: This is a description of the model structure.

claim: The postsynaptic contribution to the synaptic weight, Wpost is taken proportional to the amount of CaMKII activated by the NMDAR pathway.
source: The postsynaptic contribution to the synaptic weight, Wpost is taken proportional to the amount of CaMKII activated by the NMDAR pathway.
evidence: This is a description of the model structure.

claim: The model exhibits bistable dynamics between a down state where CaMKII is inactive and an up state where CaMKII is highly activated.
source: This part of our model (from Graupner and Brunel, 2007) exhibits bistable dynamics between a down state where CaMKII is inactive and an up state where CaMKII is highly activated (Figure 2B1).
evidence: This describes model behavior shown in Figure 2B1.

claim: The level of activated CaMKII needs 50–60 post-pre pairings (with ΔtSTDP=-15 ms) to reach the threshold between the up and down states.
source: Importantly, the level of activated CaMKII needs 50–60 post-pre pairings (with ΔtSTDP=-15 ms) to reach the threshold between the up and down states (Figure 2B1).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model shown in Figure 2B1.

claim: Wpost converges to the up state (potentiation) only when Npairings>50 post-pre pairings.
source: As a result, Wpost converges to the up state (potentiation) only when Npairings>50 post-pre pairings, thus emulating the experimental observations of NMDAR-dependent LTP and its dependence on the number of pairings (Cui et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model that matches experimental observations.

claim: For pre-post pairings, the calcium response after each pairing activates less of the CaMKII-activating calmodulin so the amount of activated CaMKII never reaches the threshold for the up state.
source: For pre-post pairings, the calcium response after each pairing activates less of the CaMKII-activating calmodulin (Figure 2C) so the amount of activated CaMKII never reaches the threshold for the up state (Figure 2B2).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model shown in Figures 2B2 and 2C.

claim: The model predicts no NMDAR-dependent plasticity for pre-post pairings (0<Npairings<100 at 1 Hz).
source: Thus, the model predicts no NMDAR-dependent for pre-post pairings (0<Npairings<100 at 1 Hz, Figure 2C2), in agreement with experimental observations (Cui et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model that matches experimental observations.

claim: The amplitude of the calcium peaks triggered by each paired stimulation shows a peculiar biphasic envelope: calcium first increases for the first 10–20 pairings then decreases afterwards, until it reaches constant amplitude after 50 pairings.
source: Within a wide parameter range, the amplitude of the calcium peaks triggered by each paired stimulation shows a peculiar biphasic envelope (Figure 3A): calcium first increases for the first 10–20 pairings then decreases afterwards, until it reaches constant amplitude after 50 pairings.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model shown in Figure 3A.

claim: During the first 10–20 pairings, repeated activation of mGluRs progressively increases the quantity of IP3, which contributes an extra influx of calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: During the first 10–20 pairings, repeated activation of mGluRs progressively increases the quantity of IP3, which contributes an extra influx of calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation from the mathematical model.

claim: The boost of cytoplasmic calcium progressively disappears when Npairings increases further because the concentration of calcium in the endoplasmic reticulum decreases.
source: This boost of cytoplasmic calcium however progressively disappears when Npairings increases further because the concentration of calcium in the endoplasmic reticulum decreases.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation from the mathematical model.

claim: The width of the postsynaptic calcium peak in the model is larger with post-pre than pre-post pairings.
source: Moreover, after each pairing, the width of the postsynaptic calcium peak in the model is larger with post-pre than pre-post pairings (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The fraction of calcium-activated DAGLα is significant only for small values of |ΔtSTDP| (<25 ms) and larger for post-pre than pre-post pairings.
source: As a consequence, the fraction of calcium-activated DAGLα is significant only for small values of |ΔtSTDP| (<25 ms) and larger for post-pre than pre-post pairings.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: The biphasic envelope of the calcium peak amplitude with Npairings is transmitted to the amplitude of eCB transients and, ultimately, to CB1R activation (yCB1R).
source: As a result, the biphasic envelope of the calcium peak amplitude with Npairings (first increase, then decrease) is transmitted to the amplitude of eCB transients and, ultimately, to CB1R activation (yCB1R).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: The biphasic envelope is even more marked at the level of CB1R activation because of CB1R desensitization that amplifies the decay above 20 pairings.
source: The biphasic envelope is even more marked at the level of CB1R activation because of CB1R desensitization that amplifies the decay above 20 pairings.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: yCB1R reaches large values only for short post-pre pairings (ΔtSTDP around -15 ms) while even short pre-post pairings (0<ΔtSTDP<10 ms) do not give rise to such large amplitude peaks.
source: yCB1R reaches large values only for short post-pre pairings (ΔtSTDP around -15 ms) while even short pre-post pairings (0<ΔtSTDP<10 ms) do not give rise to such large amplitude peaks.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The mechanism proposed by the mathematical model to account for eCB-STDP is that eCB-tLTD requires moderate levels of CB1R activation, which can be reached with pre-post pairings; eCB-tLTP demands higher levels of CB1R activation that are reached only with 5–30 post-pre pairings.
source: In conclusion, the mechanism proposed by our mathematical model to account for eCB-STDP is the following: eCB-tLTD requires moderate levels of CB1R activation, which can be reached with pre-post pairings; eCB-tLTP demands higher levels of CB1R activation that are reached only with 5–30 post-pre pairings, where every component of the model contributes maximally to CB1R activation (maximal cytosolic calcium influx from NMDAR, VSCC, TRPV1 and maximal calcium efflux from internal stores, combined with a minimal CB1R desensitization).
evidence: This is a summary of the mechanistic hypothesis from the mathematical model.

claim: Beyond 30 post-pre pairings, calcium efflux from the internal calcium stores decreases while in parallel CB1R desensitization increases, causing CB1R activation to become insufficient to maintain the elevation of the synaptic weight, so that eCB-tLTP vanishes.
source: Beyond 30 post-pre pairings, calcium efflux from the internal calcium stores decreases while in parallel CB1R desensitization increases. CB1R activation becomes insufficient to maintain the elevation of the synaptic weight, so that eCB-tLTP vanishes.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation from the mathematical model.

claim: The mathematical model correctly accounts for a plasticity gap for 40–60 post-pre pairings that isolates the two LTP domains in agreement with experimental observations.
source: Note that the model correctly accounts for a plasticity gap for 40–60 post-pre pairings that isolates the two LTP domains in agreement with experimental observations (Cui et al., 2015)
evidence: This is a comparison between model predictions and experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The expression of plasticity does not change when Npairings>100.
source: and that the expression of plasticity does not change when Npairings>100 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Model predictions match experiments quantitatively for the amplitude and sign of plasticity, as well as for the dependence of plasticity on spike timing.
source: Quantitative agreement is found for the amplitude and sign of plasticity, as well as for the dependence of plasticity on spike timing.
evidence: This is a comparison between model predictions and experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The present model is the first mathematical model able to account for the outcome of the plasticity when both ΔtSTDP and Npairings are varied.
source: To our knowledge, the present model is the first mathematical model able to account for the outcome of the plasticity when both ΔtSTDP and Npairings are varied.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the model based on comparison with existing literature.

claim: In the NMDAR signaling knockout model, the post-pre NMDAR-dependent LTP is absent, but pre-post tLTD and post-pre tLTP (observed with low numbers of pairings: 5<Npairings<35) are conserved.
source: As expected, the post-pre NDMAR-dependent LTP is absent in this NMDAR signaling knockout model, but pre-post tLTD and post-pre tLTP (observed with low numbers of pairings: 5<Npairings<35) are conserved (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a prediction from the in-silico knockout model shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Comparison with experimental data where NMDAR signaling was blocked with D-AP5 or CaMKII with KN62 confirms the match between model and experiments.
source: Comparison with experimental data where NMDAR signaling was blocked with D-AP5 or CaMKI with KN62 confirms the match between model and experiments (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a comparison between model predictions and experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In the CB1R in-silico knockout model, the only remaining plasticity domain is the LTP expressed for post-pre pairings (Npairings>50).
source: In this case, the only remaining plasticity domain is the LTP expressed for post-pre pairings (Npairings>50).
evidence: This is a prediction from the in-silico knockout model shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The model with smooth thresholds for eCB-dependent plasticity yields output very similar to that obtained with sharp thresholds.
source: Even without changing any of the model parameters outside the threshold function, the model output with such smooth thresholds is very similar to the one obtained with the sharp threshold of Equation 1 (compare with Figure 4A1).
evidence: This is a sensitivity analysis result shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The most sensitive parameters in the model were those related to reactions that are known from pharmacological experiments to be crucial to STDP.
source: As expected, the most sensitive parameters were those related to reactions that are known from pharmacological experiments to be indeed crucial to STDP: the total amount of Calmodulin or CaMKII (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), post-synaptic calcium buffering (Fino et al., 2010; Cui et al., 2015), TRPV1 and NMDA channels (Fino et al., 2010; Cui et al., 2015), DAGLipase activity (Cui et al., 2015) or FAAH and MAGLipase activity (see below).
evidence: This is a result from sensitivity analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The model was sensitive to the dynamics of CB1R desensitization, in agreement with the importance of CB1R desensitization in the decay of eCB-LTP above 15–20 post-pre stimulations.
source: The model was also found sensitive to the dynamics of CB1R desensitization, in agreement with the importance of CB1R desensitization in the decay of eCB-LTP above 15–20 post-pre stimulations.
evidence: This is a result from sensitivity analysis.

claim: The model was sensitive to the value of the threshold for eCB-LTP induction.
source: The model was also sensitive to the value of the threshold for eCB-LTP induction (whether smooth or sharp).
evidence: This is a result from sensitivity analysis.

claim: The model was sensitive to the dynamics of glutamate in the synaptic cleft (decay rate τG).
source: More surprising is the sensitivity of the model to the dynamics of glutamate in the synaptic cleft (decay rate τG).
evidence: This is a result from sensitivity analysis.

claim: Alterations of the dynamics of glutamate release and uptake can be expected to play an important role in the control of STDP at the corticostriatal synapse.
source: Alterations of the dynamics of glutamate release and uptake can thus be expected to play an important role in the control of STDP at the corticostriatal synapse.
evidence: This is inferred from the sensitivity analysis results.

claim: When frequency increases above 1 Hz, the eCB-tLTP triggered by post-pre stimulations (ΔtSTDP<0) persists and is even observed for an increasingly large ΔtSTDP range.
source: When frequency increases above 1 Hz, the eCB-tLTP triggered by post-pre stimulations (ΔtSTDP<0) persists and is even observed for an increasingly large ΔtSTDP range.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The model predicts the expression of another tLTP, triggered by 10 pre-post stimulations (ΔtSTDP>0) for frequency larger than 2 Hz.
source: The model also predicts the expression of another tLTP, triggered by 10 pre-post stimulations (ΔtSTDP>0) for frequency larger than 2 Hz.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model shown in Figure 5A.

claim: 10 post-pre pairings at 0.1 Hz were able to induce tLTP (133±14, n=10, p=0.0386).
source: 10 post-pre pairings at 0.1 Hz were able to induce tLTP (133±14, n=10, p=0.0386) (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: tLTP induced by 10 post-pre pairings at 0.1 Hz was not significantly different from eCB-tLTP induced with 10 pairings at 1 Hz (p=0.1538).
source: which was not significantly different from eCB-tLTP induced with 10 pairings at 1 Hz (p=0.1538) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison of experimental data.

claim: At frequencies >1 Hz, tLTP was observed for 10 post-pre pairings at 2.5 Hz (161±15, n=23, p=0.0004) and 4 Hz (165±14, n=22, p=0.0001).
source: At frequencies >1 Hz, we observed tLTP for 10 post-pre pairings at 2.5 Hz (161±15, n=23, p=0.0004) and 4 Hz (165±14, n=22, p=0.0001)
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: At frequencies >1 Hz, tLTP was observed for pre-post pairings at 2.5 Hz (130±14, n=12, p=0.0490 for ΔtSTDP<+50 ms; 119±9, n=20, p=0.060 for ΔtSTDP<+100 ms) and 4 Hz (139±13, n=10, p=0.0150).
source: but also for pre-post pairings at 2.5 Hz (130±14, n=12, p=0.0490 for ΔtSTDP<+50 ms; 119±9, n=20, p=0.060 for ΔtSTDP<+100 ms) and 4 Hz (139±13, n=10, p=0.0150).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: The ΔtSTDP range for tLTP induction was considerably enlarged for post-pre pairings: from -30<ΔtSTDP<0 ms at 1 Hz to -100<ΔtSTDP<0 ms at 2.5 or 4 Hz.
source: Moreover, the ΔtSTDP range for tLTP induction was considerably enlarged for post-pre pairings: from -30<ΔtSTDP<0 ms at 1 Hz to -100<ΔtSTDP<0 ms at 2.5 or 4 Hz.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: For pre-post pairings, tLTP could be observed for ΔtSTDP<+50 ms.
source: Note that for pre-post pairings, tLTP could be observed for ΔtSTDP<+50 ms (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: When the frequency of the pairings was increased to 2.5 or 4 Hz, a symmetric Hebbian plasticity was observed, i.e. the induction of tLTP not only for post-pre but also for pre-post pairings.
source: Therefore, when we increased the frequency of the pairings to 2.5 or 4 Hz, our experimental results show a very good match with the prediction of the model: we observed first a symmetric Hebbian plasticity, i.e. the induction of tLTP not only for post-pre but also for pre-post pairings
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5D and E that matches model predictions.

claim: At 2.5 and 4 Hz, an enlargement of the range of ΔtSTDP in which plasticity was observed occurred.
source: and, secondly an enlargement of the range of ΔtSTDP in which plasticity was observed.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5D and E that matches model predictions.

claim: For 2.5 and 4 Hz STDP, post-pre tLTP was not prevented with AM251 (3 μM) (150±11, n=6, p=0.0069) or with D-AP5 (50 μM) (135±12, n=11, p=0.013) but was precluded with a mixture of both AM251 and D-AP5 (96±3, n=9, p=0.1800).
source: We observed that for 2.5 and 4 Hz STDP, post-pre tLTP was not prevented with AM251 (3 μM) (150±11, n=6, p=0.0069) or with D-AP5 (50 μM) (135±12, n=11, p=0.013) but was precluded with a mixture of both AM251 and D-AP5 (96±3, n=9, p=01800).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: For pre-post pairings at 2.5 and 4 Hz, tLTP was still observed with AM251 (149±15, n=7, p=0.0178) but was prevented with D-AP5 (134±27, n=5, p=0.2684) or a mixture of AM251 and D-AP5 (88±11, n=3, p=0.4090).
source: Similarly, for pre-post pairings at 2.5 and 4 Hz, tLTP was still observed with AM251 (149±15, n=7, p=0.0178) but was prevented with D-AP5 (134±27, n=5, p=0.2684) or a mixture of AM251 and D-AP5 (88±11, n=3, p=0.4090).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: At frequencies above 1 Hz, the tLTP triggered by 10–15 post-pre or pre-post pairings becomes both eCB and NMDAR-dependent.
source: Therefore, model predictions and experiments provide converging suggestion that at frequencies above 1 Hz, the tLTP triggered by 10–15 post-pre or pre-post pairings becomes both eCB and NMDAR-dependent.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from both model predictions and experimental data.

claim: 100 puffs of 2-AG at low concentration (20 μM) induced a significant LTD (65±5%, p=0.0009, n=6) with magnitude similar to the tLTD induced by 100 pre-post pairings (p=0.9340).
source: We observed that in the absence of STDP protocol, 100 puffs of 2-AG were able to induce a significant LTD (65±5%, p=0.0009, n=6) (Figure 6A1 and 6A2) with magnitude similar to the tLTD induced by 100 pre-post pairings (FigFigure 1D2) (p=0.9340).
evidence: This is experimental data from 2-AG puff experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: 10 puffs of low [2-AG] (20 μM) did not induce significant plasticity (95±11%, p=0.6931, n=6).
source: When we delivered 10 puffs of low [2-AG] (20 μM), no significant plasticity was detected (95±11%, p=0.6931, n=6) (Figure 6B1 and 6B2).
evidence: This is experimental data from 2-AG puff experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: 100 puffs of high [2-AG] (100 μM) induced a potent LTD (61±7%, p=0.0021, n=7) with magnitude similar to the tLTD induced by 100 pre-post pairings (p=0.6676).
source: After applying 100 puffs of 100 µM 2-AG, a potent LTD was observed (61±7%, p=0.0021, n=7) (Figure 6C1 and 6C2) with magnitude similar to the tLTD induced by 100 pre-post pairings (Figure 1D2) (p=0.6676).
evidence: This is experimental data from 2-AG puff experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claim: LTD induced by 100 puffs of high [2-AG] (100 μM) was CB1R-mediated because it was prevented by AM251 (3 μM) (94±5%, p=0.2817, n=5).
source: We verified that this LTD was CB1R-mediated by preventing plasticity with AM251 (3 μM) (94±5%, p=0.2817, n=5) (Figure 6C2).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 6C2.

claim: 10 puffs of high [2-AG] (100 μM) induced a potent LTP (168±29%, p=0.0106, n=5) with magnitude similar to the tLTP induced by 10 post-pre pairings (p=0.0106).
source: Strikingly, 10 puffs of high[2-AG] (100 μM) induced a potent LTP (168±29%, p=0.0106, n=5) (Figure 6D1 and 6D2) with magnitude similar to the tLTP induced by 10 post-pre pairings (Figure 1E2) (p=0.0106).
evidence: This is experimental data from 2-AG puff experiments shown in Figure 6D.

claim: LTP induced by 10 puffs of high [2-AG] (100 μM) was CB1R-mediated because when CB1R was inhibited with AM251 (3 μM), 10 puffs of [2-AG] (100 μM) did not induce significant plasticity (92±4%, p=0.1542, n=5).
source: This LTP was CB1R-mediated because when CB1R was inhibited with AM251 (3 μM), 10 puffs of [2-AG] (100 μM) did not induce significant plasticity (92±4%, p=0.1542, n=5) (Figure 6D2).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 6D2.

claim: 100 puffs of low or high [2-AG] induce LTD while only high [2-AG] succeeds to trigger LTP, thus validating the model prediction.
source: Therefore, 100 puffs of low or high [2-AG] induce LTD while only high [2-AG] succeeds to trigger LTP, thus validating the model prediction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 2-AG puff experiments that validates model predictions.

claim: Five post-pre pairings is the lowest number of pairings needed to induce significant eCB-tLTP (134±13%, p=0.0190, n=17).
source: 5Five pairings appearas the lowest number of pairings needed to induce significant eCB-tLTP as illustrated by the representative and average STDP (134±13%, p=0.0190, n=17) (Figure 7B and D)
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 7B and D.

claim: The model faithfully predicted eCB-tLTP for 5 post-pre pairings.
source: Note that the model also faithfully predicted eCB-tLTP for such number of pairings (Figure 4A and 7A).
evidence: This is a comparison between model predictions and experimental data shown in Figures 4A and 7A.

claim: Inhibition of the MAGL with JZL184 (1.5 μM) significantly increased the magnitude of eCB-tLTP induced by 5 post-pre pairings (182±17%, p=0.0048, n=6; p=0.0294 when compared to 5 post-pre pairings in control conditions).
source: As predicted by the model, inhibition of the MAGL with JZL184 (1.5 μM) significantly increased the magnitude of eCB-tLTP (182±17%, p=0.0048, n=6; p=0.0294 when compared to 5 post-pre pairings in control conditions) (Figure 7: with an example of LTP induced by five 5 post-pre pairings at ΔtSTDP=-19 ms in B, with an example of LTP induced by five post-pre pairings at ΔtSTDP=-18 ms with JZL184 in C and the experiment summary in D).
evidence: This is experimental data from MAGL inhibition experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: The amplification of eCB-tLTP by MAGL inhibition was CB1R-mediated since no plasticity was observed when CB1R were blocked by AM251 (3 μM) (96±8%, p=0.6123, n=5).
source: We confirmed that this amplification was CB1R-mediated since no plasticity was observed when CB1R were blocked by AM251 (3 μM) (96±8%, p=0.6123, n=5) (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Bath-applied JZL treatment in the absence of STDP pairings did not induce significant plasticity (96±7%, p=0.5943, n=5).
source: We also ensured that bath-applied JZL treatment in the absence of STDP pairings did not induce significant plasticity (96±7%, p=0.5943, n=5).
evidence: This is experimental data from control experiments.

claim: The occurrence of eCB-tLTP was higher with MAGL inhibition: in control, five post-pre pairings yielded 60% of eCB-tLTP (10/17 cells showed significant tLTP) while with MAGL inhibition, 100% of the recorded cells displayed eCB-tLTP (6/6 cells displayed significant tLTP).
source: It should be noted that the occurrence of eCB-tLTP was also higher with MAGL inhibition: in control, five post-pre pairings yielded 60% of eCB-tLTP (10/17 cells showed significant tLTP) while with MAGL inhibition, 100% of the recorded cells displayed eCB-tLTP (6/6 cells displayed significant tLTP).
evidence: This is experimental data comparing control and MAGL inhibition conditions.

claim: 50 post-pre pairings failed to induce any plasticity in control conditions (101±7%, p=0.9030, n=13).
source: Experimentally, as previously reported (Cui et al., 2015), STDP protocols with 50 post-pre pairings failed to induce any plasticity in control conditions as illustrated by the representative and average STDP (101±7%, p=0.9030, n=13) (Figure 8B and D; with an example of an absence of plasticity for 50 post-pre pairings at ΔtSTDP=-20 ms in B and the experiment summary in D).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 8B and D.

claim: 50 post-pre pairings under inhibition of MAGL with JZL184 (1.5 μM) induced tLTP (139±15%, p=0.0248, n=9).
source: As predicted by the model, we found that 50 post-pre pairings under inhibition of MAGL with JZL184 (1.5 μM) induced tLTP (139±15%, p=0.0248, n=9) (Figure 8C and D; with an example of tLTP induced by 50 post-pre pairings at ΔtSTDP=-16 ms with JZL184 and the experiment summary in D).
evidence: This is experimental data from MAGL inhibition experiments shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: tLTP induced by 50 post-pre pairings under MAGL inhibition was eCB-mediated since suppressed by AM251 (3 μM) (93±4%, p=0.3365, n=5).
source: This tLTP was eCB-mediated since suppressed by AM251 (3 μM) (93±4%, p=0.3365, n=5) (Figure 8D2).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 8D2.

claim: By acting on the 2-AG levels, it was possible to trigger eCB-tLTP for an activity pattern which does not generate LTP in control conditions.
source: Therefore, by acting on the 2-AG levels, we were able to trigger eCB-tLTP for an activity pattern, which does not generate LTP in control conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the MAGL inhibition experiments with 50 post-pre pairings.

claim: 100 presynaptic stimulations (without postsynaptic pairing) induced LTD (76±9%, p=0.0337, n=8), which was CB1R-mediated since prevented with AM251 (3 μM) (102±7%, p=0.8108, n=4).
source: Experimentally, 100 presynaptic stimulations (without postsynaptic pairing) induced LTD (76±9%, p=0.0337, n=8), which was CB1R-mediated since prevented with AM251 (3 μM) (102±7%, p=0.8108, n=4) (Figure 9B; with an example of LTD induced by 100 pre stimulations in B1 and the experiment summary in B2)
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: When 2-AG levels were amplified by MAGL inhibition with JZL184 (1.5 μM), 100 pre-synaptic stimulations triggered LTP (143±17%, p=0.0299, n=11) instead of LTD in control conditions.
source: In agreement with the model, when 2-AG levels were amplified by MAGL inhibition with JZL184 (1.5 μM), 100 pre-synaptic stimulations triggered LTP (143±17%, p=0.0299, n=11) instead of LTD in control conditions (Figure 9C; with an example of tLTP induced by 100 pre stimulations with JZL184 in C1 and the experiment summary in 9C2).
evidence: This is experimental data from MAGL inhibition experiments shown in Figure 9C.

claim: tLTP induced by 100 presynaptic stimulations under MAGL inhibition was eCB-mediated since it was prevented when JZL184 was co-applied with AM251 (3 μM) (93±4%, p=0.1509, n=5).
source: This tLTP was eCB-mediated since it was prevented when JZL184 was co-applied with AM251 (3 μM) (93±4%, p=0.1509, n=5) (Figure 9C2).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 9C2.

claim: Manipulating the activity of the MAGL was sufficient to (1) control the magnitude of eCB-tLTP, (2) induce eCB-tLTP or (3) reverse eCB-LTD into eCB-tLTP.
source: To summarize, manipulating the activity of the MAGL was sufficient to (1) control the magnitude of eCB-tLTP, (2) induce eCB-tLTP or (3) even to reverse eCB-LTD into eCB-tLTP.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from MAGL inhibition experiments.

claim: 2-AG levels control eCB plasticity in a bidirectional way, with large 2-AG levels yielding eCB-tLTP and lower levels eCB-tLTD.
source: These experimental validations of the model predictions thus support our model hypothesis that 2-AG levels control eCB plasticity in a bidirectional way, with large 2-AG levels yielding eCB-tLTP and lower levels eCB-tLTD.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental validations of model predictions.

claim: Inhibition of PKA by bath-applied inhibitor KT5720 (1 μM) during a STDP protocol that triggers eCB-tLTD in control condition (100 pre-post pairings) did not affect the expression of eCB-tLTD (74±10%, p=0.020, n=5; p=0.8752 compared to control tLTD).
source: Inhibition of PKA by bath-applied inhibitor KT5720 (1 μM) during a STDP protocol that triggers eCB-tLTD in control condition (100 pre-post pairings) did not affect the expression of eCB-tLTD (74±10%, p=0.020, n=5; p=0.8752 compared to control tLTD) (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 10A.

claim: CaN inhibition by cyclosporin A (1 μM) prevented eCB-tLTD (122±18%, p=0.2560, n=6).
source: We found that CaN inhibition by cyclosporin A (1 μM) prevented eCB-tLTD (122±18%, p=0.2560, n=6) (Figure 10A2 and 10B)
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 10A2 and 10B.

claim: Bath-applied CaN inhibitor cyclosporin A did not preclude the expression of eCB-tLTP induced with 10 post-pre pairings (154±17%, p=0.0305, n=5).
source: Bath-applied CaN inhibitor cyclosporin A did not preclude the expression of eCB-tLTP (154±17%, p=0.0305, n=5) (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Inhibition of PKA with KT5720 (1 μM) prevented plasticity with 10 post-pre pairings (98±2%, p=0.3203, n=4) demonstrating that PKA activity is critically involved in eCB-tLTP.
source: Inhibition of PKA with KT5720 (1 μM) prevented plasticity with 10 post-pre pairings (98±2%, p=0.3203, n=4) (Figure 10C) demonstrating that PKA activity is critically involved in eCB-tLTP.
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Intracellular application of KT5720 (i-KT5720, 1 μM) or a cell-non-permeant PKA inhibitor PKI 6–22 (i-PKI 6–22, 20 μM) did not significantly affect eCB-tLTP (with i-KT5720: 137±8%, p=0.0108, n=5; with i-PKI 6–22: 163±29%, p=0.03249, n=7).
source: For this purpose, we restricted PKA inhibition to the postsynaptic neuron with intracellular application (through the patch-clamp pipette) of KT5720 (i-KT5720, 1 μM) or a cell-non-permeant PKA inhibitor PKI 6–22 (i-PKI 6–22, 20 μM). Both treatments did not significantly affect eCB-tLTP (with i-KT5720: 137±8%, p=0.0108, n=5; with i-PKI 6–22: 163±29%, p=0.03249, n=7) (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is experimental data from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 10C.

claim: The activity of presynaptic PKA is critical for the expression of eCB-tLTP.
source: We therefore conclude that the activity of presynaptic PKA is critical for the expression of eCB-tLTP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological experiments with PKA inhibitors.

claim: The expression of eCB-tLTD at the corticostriatal synapse depends on the activity of CaN (and possibly on PKA inhibition).
source: Together, these results suggest that the expression of eCB-tLTD at the corticostriatal synapse depends on the activity of CaN (Figure 10B) (and possibly on PKA inhibition)
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 10B.

claim: The expression of eCB-tLTP is conditioned by the activity of presynaptic PKA.
source: whereas the expression of eCB-tLTP is conditioned by the activity of presynaptic PKA (Figure 10D).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 10D.

claim: Intermediate levels of CB1R activation trigger eCB-tLTD through a combination of PKA inhibition and CaN activity, whereas high levels of CB1R activation leads to eCB-tLTP through the reverse combination: PKA activity combined to CaN inhibition.
source: Therefore, intermediate levels of CB1R activation trigger eCB-tLTD through a combination of PKA inhibition and CaN activity, whereas high levels of CB1R activation leads to eCB-tLTP through the reverse combination: PKA activity combined to CaN inhibition.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis inferred from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: Long-term synaptic changes at corticostriatal synapses provide fundamental mechanisms for the function of the basal ganglia in action selection and in procedural learning.
source: Long-term synaptic changes at corticostriatal synapses provide fundamental mechanisms for the function of the basal ganglia in action selection and in procedural learning (Yin et al., 2009)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: eCB plasticity has emerged as the major form underlying long-term synaptic strength changes at corticostriatal synapses.
source: in which eCB plasticity have emerged as the major form underlying long-term synaptic strength changes (Mathur et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: eCB dynamics tightly control both the induction/maintenance and polarity of synaptic weight changes in a paired-activity dependent manner.
source: We describe here a paired-activity dependent tLTP and tLTD, wherein eCB dynamics tightly control both the induction/maintenance and polarity of synaptic weight changes.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: Due to their on-demand intercellular signaling modus operandi, eCB biosynthesis and release are evoked by precisely timed physiological stimuli.
source: Due to their on-demand intercellular signaling modus operandi (Alger and Kim, 2011), eCB biosynthesis and release are evoked by precisely timed physiological stimuli.
evidence: This is established knowledge about eCB signaling supported by citation.

claim: STDP, an important physiological form of Hebbian plasticity, efficiently triggers eCB signaling.
source: Our study demonstrates that STDP, an important physiological form of Hebbian plasticity, efficiently triggers eCB signaling
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study findings.

claim: eCB signaling controls the STDP polarity in a bidirectional manner depending on the activity pattern.
source: and that eCB signaling controls the STDP polarity in a bidirectional manner depending on the activity pattern.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study findings.

claim: The manipulation of MAGL activity may bootstrap synaptic plasticity in synapses where the postsynaptic neuron is silent, thus rescuing possible pathological situations or waking up new local circuits.
source: This discovery may have far-reaching consequences, since it means that the manipulation of MAGL activity may bootstrap synaptic plasticity in synapses where the postsynaptic neuron is silent, thus rescuing possible pathological situations or waking up new local circuits.
evidence: This is a speculative implication of the findings about MAGL inhibition.

claim: Nerve growth factor (NGF) signaling in cholinergic projection neurons of fetal mice has been shown to control MAGL degradation in vivo and in vitro in a spatially specific way.
source: it is noteworthy that recently, nerve growth factor (NGF) signaling in cholinergic projection neurons of fetal mice has been shown to control MAGL degradation in vivo and in vitro in a spatially specific way (Keimpema et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The regulation of MAGL activity may be a potent mechanism to control synaptic plasticity and thus learning and memory.
source: In light of our findings, these results suggest that the regulation of MAGL activity may indeed be a potent mechanism to control synaptic plasticity and thus learning and memory.
evidence: This is a speculative implication inferred from the study findings and previous literature.

claim: Short puffs of highly concentrated 2-AG yields LTP in the absence of any electrical stimulation, which is a strong argument in favor of the model-derived hypothesis that eCB can support tLTP in addition to tLTD.
source: Our experimental results showing that short puffs of highly concentrated 2-AG yields LTP in the absence of any electrical stimulation is a strong argument in favor of the model-derived hypothesis that eCB can support tLTP in addition to tLTD.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 2-AG puff experiments that supports the model hypothesis.

claim: Both the amplitude (≃165%) and the pharmacology (suppression by CB1R antagonist AM251) of the LTP observed with 2-AG puffs are identical to those observed for tLTP triggered by 10 post-pre pairings.
source: Both the amplitude (≃165%) and the pharmacology (suppression by CB1R antagonist AM251) of the LTP observed with these puffs are identical to those observed for tLTP triggered by 10 post-pre pairings.
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data from 2-AG puffs and STDP experiments.

claim: When 2-AG is applied in the form of prolonged puffs (x100), LTD is observed instead of LTP, which according to the mathematical model would be due to desensitization of the CB1R that becomes prominent with prolonged puffs.
source: Moreover, it is important to note that when we applied 2-AG in the form of prolonged puffs (x100), we observed LTD instead of LTP. According to our mathematical model, this behavior would be due to desensitization of the CB1R that becomes prominent with prolonged puffs.
evidence: This is an experimental observation explained by the mathematical model.

claim: 2-AG puff application is generally expected to give rise to depression except if the puffs are of short duration, where potentiation can be observed.
source: 2-AG puff application is therefore generally expected to give rise to depression except if the puffs are of short duration, where potentiation can be observed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 2-AG puff experiments and model predictions.

claim: The widespread observation that prolonged applications of 2-AG systematically yielded to LTD might be explained by CB1R desensitization with prolonged applications.
source: This feature may account for the widespread observation that prolonged applications of 2-AG systematically yielded to LTD and might explain why eCB-dependent potentiation has proven difficult to observe experimentally.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for previous experimental observations based on the current findings.

claim: The mathematical model shows very good agreement with experimental data, even for conditions for which the model was not fitted (stimulation frequency >1 Hz, alteration of MAGLipase activity).
source: Our mathematical model in general shows very good agreement with experimental data, even for conditions for which the model was not fitted (stimulation frequency >1 Hz, alteration of MAGLipase activity).
evidence: This is an assessment of the model's predictive power.

claim: 100 presynaptic stimulations at 1 Hz, in the absence of post-synaptic stimulation, are sufficient to trigger eCB-LTD experimentally, likely due to the production of eCB resulting from the postsynaptic depolarization triggered by the 100 presynaptic stimulations (depolarization-induced LTD).
source: For instance, Figure 9B shows that 100 presynaptic stimulations at 1 Hz, in the absence of post-synaptic stimulation, are sufficient to trigger eCB-LTD experimentally. This is likely due to the production of eCB resulting from the postsynaptic depolarization triggered by the 100 presynaptic stimulations (depolarization-induced LTD).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with a mechanistic explanation.

claim: In the model, the postsynaptic depolarization triggered by 100 presynaptic stimulations at 1 Hz is not large enough to allow the entry of the minimal amount of calcium that is needed to overcome the eCB-LTD threshold, so no plasticity is observed.
source: In the model however, the postsynaptic depolarization triggered by 100 presynaptic stimulations at 1 Hz is not large enough to allow the entry of the minimal amount of calcium that is needed to overcome the eCB-LTD threshold, so no plasticity is observed.
evidence: This is a description of a mismatch between model predictions and experimental observations.

claim: The dynamics of glutamate release and binding are expected to be crucial for the expression of STDP.
source: The dynamics of glutamate release and binding are expected to be crucial for the expression of STDP, as illustrated by our sensitivity analysis (Figure 4).
evidence: This is inferred from the sensitivity analysis results.

claim: Several parts of the glutamate release and binding machinery at the corticostriatal synapse are known to display nontrivial frequency-dependence, including presynaptic glutamate release, uptake by transporters and receptor activation because of desensitization of AMPAR.
source: Several parts of the glutamate release and binding machinery at the corticostriatal synapse are known to display nontrivial frequency-dependence, including presynaptic glutamate release, uptake by transporters and receptor activation because of desensitization of AMPAR (Goubard et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The mathematical model features none of the frequency dependencies of glutamate release and binding machinery, so a precise quantitative match between experiments and model when frequency is varied cannot be expected.
source: Since our mathematical model features none of these frequency dependencies, we cannot expect a precise quantitative match between experiments and model when frequency is varied.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the model.

claim: The model yields correct predictions of the main qualitative trends observed in the experiments when frequency is varied.
source: However, it is remarkable that the model still yields correct predictions of the main qualitative trends observed in the experiments.
evidence: This is an assessment of the model's predictive power despite its limitations.

claim: 10 post-pre pairings at very low frequency (0.1 Hz) are sufficient to trigger tLTP in the experiments, while the model predicts no plasticity at those frequencies.
source: For instance, 10 post-pre pairings at very low frequency (0.1 Hz) are sufficient to trigger tLTP in the experiments, while the model predicts no plasticity at those frequencies (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a comparison between experimental data and model predictions showing a mismatch.

claim: At 4 Hz, the experimental pharmacology profile with 10 pairings is not matched by the model with 10 pairings, but with 15 pairings.
source: At 4 Hz, the experimental pharmacology profile with 10 pairings is not matched by the model with 10 pairings, but with 15 pairings (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a comparison between experimental data and model predictions showing a mismatch.

claim: The model predictions that increased frequency should witness i) an enlarged range for the expression of tLTP with post-pre 10 pairings and ii) the emergence of a new tLTP with 10 pre-post pairings turned out to be generally correct.
source: Nevertheless, the model predictions that increased frequency should witness i) an enlarged range for the expression of tLTP with post-pre 10 pairings and ii) the emergence of a new tLTP with 10 pre-post pairings turned out to be generally correct.
evidence: This is an assessment of the model's predictive power.

claim: In the hippocampus, theta-burst stimulation induces eCB-dependent LTD at the synapse between inhibitory interneurons and pyramidal cells that is blocked when presynaptic CaN is inhibited.
source: In the hippocampus, theta-burst stimulation induces eCB-dependent LTD at the synapse between inhibitory interneurons and pyramidal cells that is blocked when presynaptic CaN is inhibited (Heifets et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: eCB-tLTD triggered at the corticostriatal synapse needs CaN activity.
source: Similarly, we found that eCB-tLTD triggered at the corticostriatal synapse also needs CaN activity.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by experimental data.

claim: In the hippocampus and nucleus accumbens, the expression of frequency-dependent eCB-LTD is blocked when cAMP levels are increased by the adenylyl-cyclase activator forskolin.
source: In the hippocampus (Chevaleyre et al, 2007) and nucleus accumbens (Mato et al., 2008), the expression of frequency-dependent eCB-LTD is blocked when cAMP levels are increased by the adenylyl-cyclase activator forskolin.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Since PKA is activated by cAMP, increased cAMP blocking eCB-LTD indicates that reduced levels of PKA are necessary for eCB-LTD.
source: Since PKA is activated by cAMP, this indicates that reduced levels of PKA are necessary for eCB-LTD.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about PKA activation.

claim: In the hippocampus and nucleus accumbens, direct inhibition of presynaptic PKA actually blocks the expression of eCB-LTD, thus showing that the implication of PKA in eCB-dependent plasticity is a complex and subtle phenomenon.
source: In both cases however, direct inhibition of presynaptic PKA actually blocks the expression of eCB-LTD, thus showing that the implication of PKA in eCB-dependent plasticity is a complex and subtle phenomenon.
evidence: This is established knowledge that highlights the complexity of PKA's role.

claim: In the case of tLTD in the dorsolateral striatum, direct PKA inhibition does not obliterate eCB-tLTD.
source: In the case of tLTD in the dorsolateral striatum, we found that direct PKA inhibition does not obliterate eCB-tLTD.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by experimental data.

claim: The result that direct PKA inhibition does not obliterate eCB-tLTD is in line with the notion that the expression of eCB-tLTD requires PKA inhibition.
source: Our result is, therefore, in line with the notion that the expression of eCB-tLTD requires PKA inhibition.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results in the context of previous knowledge.

claim: The eCB-tLTP triggered at the corticostriatal synapse by STDP protocols had the exact inverse dependence on PKA and CaN compared to eCB-tLTD.
source: Strikingly, the eCB-tLTP triggered at the corticostriatal synapse by STDP protocols had the exact inverse dependence on PKA and CaN compared to eCB-tLTD.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by experimental data.

claim: PKA inhibitors block eCB-tLTP expression whereas CaN inhibition has no effect.
source: Indeed, we found that PKA inhibitors block eCB-tLTP expression whereas CaN inhibition has no effect.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by experimental data.

claim: The expression of eCB-tLTD needs CaN (but not PKA) activity whereas the expression of eCB-tLTP demands PKA (but not CaN) activity.
source: Therefore, our study of STDP protocols at the corticostriatal synapse shows that the expression of eCB-tLTD needs CaN (but not PKA) activity whereas the expression of eCB-tLTP demands PKA (but not CaN) activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: CB1R activation inhibits PKA activity but also inhibits presynaptic VSCCs, which are expected to hamper calcium influx in the presynaptic compartment.
source: CB1R activation inhibits PKA activity but also inhibits presynaptic VSCCs (Mato et al., 2008), which are expected to hamper calcium influx in the presynaptic compartment.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: A decrease in calcium levels reduces the CaN activity.
source: Such a decrease in calcium levels reduces the CaN activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about calcium-dependent CaN activation.

claim: CB1R activation is expected to reduce both CaN and PKA activity, although the shapes (kinetics parameters) of the decays of PKA and CaN activity with increasing CB1R activation are not necessarily identical.
source: CB1R activation is expected to reduce both CaN and PKA activity, although the shapes (kinetics parameters) of the decays of PKA and CaN activity with increasing CB1R activation are not necessarily identical.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: eCB-STDP is gated by the ratio between PKA and CaN activities: large CB1R activation would produce high values of the PKA/CaN ratio yielding eCB-tLTP whereas intermediate CB1R activations would result in low values of the PKA/CaN ratio and, consequently, in eCB-tLTD.
source: Considering our experimental data, this putative mechanism suggests that eCB-STDP is gated by the ratio between PKA and CaN activities: large CB1R activation would produce high values of the PKA/CaN ratio yielding eCB-tLTP whereas intermediate CB1R activations would result in low values of the PKA/CaN ratio and, consequently, in eCB-tLTD.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis inferred from the experimental data.

claim: eCB bidirectional plasticity constitutes a versatile system, which operation may underlie a complex repertoire of learning abilities, depending on activity pattern at corticostriatal circuits and on the behavioral context.
source: Altogether, our results show that eCB bidirectional plasticity constitutes a versatile system, which operation may underlie a complex repertoire of learning abilities, depending on activity pattern at corticostriatal circuits and on the behavioral context.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about the functional implications of the findings.

source: All experiments were performed in accordance with local animal welfare committee (Center for Interdisciplinary Research in Biology and EU guidelines, directive 2010/63/EU).
